note: The two sets are nearly identical claim-for-claim; the only substantive difference is that Set B keeps the full condition 'at conclusion of specified energy balance period' on the full-points threshold claim, while Set A drops it. Both sets correctly capture the 75% brightness minimum, the 15-minute neighbor visit, the 0–100% score range, and the three Energy Balance scoring bands. Both sets are heavily padded with duplicate restatements of the same three Energy Balance facts and the brightness fact, and both use axis-label pseudo-quotes for the figure-derived point values.
remarks: Both sets repeat the same facts under multiple entity/attribute names (full points threshold vs. full points condition vs. full points requirement; reduced points range vs. condition; no points threshold vs. condition; brightness stated twice; 'linear' stated three times), so roughly half of each set is redundant. One quote is a near-miss paraphrase ('Reduced points are scored linearly' vs. source 'are scaled linearly'), and the two figure-derived point claims (100 points at 0 kWh, 0 points at -50 kWh) are supported only by axis labels rather than a real quote, though the values are consistent with Figure 10. Important facts both sets omit: positive balance = net production / negative = net consumption, the nine movie-night scores being averaged and multiplied by maximum available points, the 10:30 p.m. submission deadline, the five-neighborhood/four-house village layout, and the suspension of the Comfort Zone occupancy rule (Rule 11-1) during movie night.
